transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Alan , thank you very much for the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to first, obviously, thank Belmont University, Tom, thank you, and to all of you who are participating tonight and those of you who sent e-mail questions in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think everybody knows now we are in the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And a lot of you I think are worried about your jobs, your pensions, your retirement accounts, your ability to send your child or your grandchild to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I believe this is a final verdict on the failed economic policies of the last eight years, strongly promoted by President Bush and supported by Senator McCain, that essentially said that we should strip away regulations, consumer protections, let the market run wild, and prosperity would rain down on all of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It hasn’t worked out that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so now we’ve got to take some decisive action.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, step one was a rescue package that was passed last week.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to make sure that works properly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that means strong oversight, making sure that investors, taxpayers are getting their money back and treated as investors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It means that we are cracking down on CEOs and making sure that they’re not getting bonuses or golden parachutes as a consequence of this package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, in fact, we just found out that AIG, a company that got a bailout, just a week after they got help went on a $400,000 junket.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll tell you what, the Treasury should demand that money back and those executives should be fired.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But that’s only step one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The middle-class need a rescue package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that means tax cuts for the middle-class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It means help for homeowners so that they can stay in their homes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It means that we are helping state and local governments set up road projects and bridge projects that keep people in their jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And then long-term we’ve got to fix our health care system, we’ve got to fix our energy system that is putting such an enormous burden on families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You need somebody working for you and you’ve got to have somebody in Washington who is thinking about the middle class and not just those who can afford to hire lobbyists.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Tom.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Belmont University.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Senator Obama, it’s good to be with you at a town hall meeting.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, Alan , thank you for your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You go to the heart of America’s worries tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Americans are angry, they’re upset, and they’re a little fearful.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s our job to fix the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, I have a plan to fix this problem and it has got to do with energy independence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to stop sending $700 billion a year to countries that don’t want us very — like us very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to keep Americans’ taxes low.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: All Americans’ taxes low.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s not raise taxes on anybody today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We obviously have to stop this spending spree that’s going on in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Do you know that we’ve laid a $10 trillion debt on these young Americans who are here with us tonight, $500 billion of it we owe to China?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to have a package of reforms and it has got to lead to reform prosperity and peace in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I think that this problem has become so severe, as you know, that we’re going to have to do something about home values.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know that home values of retirees continues to decline and people are no longer able to afford their mortgage payments.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As president of the United States, Alan, I would order the secretary of the treasury to immediately buy up the bad home loan mortgages in America and renegotiate at the new value of those homes — at the diminished value of those homes and let people be able to make those — be able to make those payments and stay in their homes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Is it expensive?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we all know, my friends, until we stabilize home values in America, we’re never going to start turning around and creating jobs and fixing our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to give some trust and confidence back to America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know how the do that, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s my proposal, it’s not Senator Obama’s proposal, it’s not President Bush’s proposal.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I know how to get America working again, restore our economy and take care of working Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Not you, Tom.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, that’s a tough question and there’s a lot of qualified Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I think the first criteria, Tom, would have to be somebody who immediately Americans identify with, immediately say, we can trust that individual.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: A supporter of Senator Obama’s is Warren Buffett.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He has already weighed in and helped stabilize some of the difficulties in the markets and with companies and corporations, institutions today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I like Meg Whitman, she knows what it’s like to be out there in the marketplace.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She knows how to create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Meg Whitman was CEO of a company that started with 12 people and is now 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: 3 million people in America make their living off eBay.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Maybe somebody here has done a little business with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the point is it’s going to have to be somebody who inspires trust and confidence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Because the problem in America today to a large extent, Tom, is that we don’t have trust and confidence in our institutions because of the corruption on Wall Street and the greed and excess and the cronyism in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Warren would be a pretty good choice — Warren Buffett, and I’m pleased to have his support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there are other folks out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The key is making sure that the next treasury secretary understands that it’s not enough just to help those at the top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Prosperity is not just going to trickle down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to help the middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve — you know, Senator McCain and I have some fundamental disagreements on the economy, starting with Senator McCain’s statement earlier that he thought the fundamentals of the economy were sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Part of the problem here is that for many of you, wages and incomes have flat-lined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: For many of you, it is getting harder and harder to save, harder and harder to retire.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why, for example, on tax policy, what I want to do is provide a middle class tax cut to 95 percent of working Americans, those who are working two jobs, people who are not spending enough time with their kids, because they are struggling to make ends meet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain is right that we’ve got to stabilize housing prices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But underlying that is loss of jobs and loss of income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s something that the next treasury secretary is going to have to work on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Oliver, and that’s an excellent question, because as you just described it, bailout, when I believe that it’s rescue, because — because of the greed and excess in Washington and Wall Street, Main Street was paying a very heavy price, and we know that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I left my campaign and suspended it to go back to Washington to make sure that there were additional protections for the taxpayer in the form of good oversight, in the form of taxpayers being the first to be paid back when our economy recovers — and it will recover — and a number of other measures.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But you know, one of the real catalysts, really the match that lit this fire was Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ll bet you, you may never even have heard of them before this crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But you know, they’re the ones that, with the encouragement of Senator Obama and his cronies and his friends in Washington, that went out and made all these risky loans, gave them to people that could never afford to pay back.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And you know, there were some of us that stood up two years ago and said we’ve got to enact legislation to fix this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to stop this greed and excess.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Meanwhile, the Democrats in the Senate and some — and some members of Congress defended what Fannie and Freddie were doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They resisted any change.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Meanwhile, they were getting all kinds of money in campaign contributions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama was the second highest recipient of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac money in history — in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So this rescue package means that we will stabilize markets, we will shore up these institutions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But it’s not enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we’re going to have to go out into the housing market and we’re going to have to buy up these bad loans and we’re going to have to stabilize home values, and that way, Americans, like Alan, can realize the American dream and stay in their home.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But Fannie and Freddie were the catalysts, the match that started this forest fire.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There were some of us — there were some of us that stood up against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There were others who took a hike.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Oliver, first, let me tell you what’s in the rescue package for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Right now, the credit markets are frozen up and what that means, as a practical matter, is that small businesses and some large businesses just can’t get loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If they can’t get a loan, that means that they can’t make payroll.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If they can’t make payroll, then they may end up having to shut their doors and lay people off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if you imagine just one company trying to deal with that, now imagine a million companies all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So it could end up having an adverse effect on everybody, and that’s why we had to take action.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we shouldn’t have been there in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’ve got to correct a little bit of Senator McCain’s history, not surprisingly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s, first of all, understand that the biggest problem in this whole process was the deregulation of the financial system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain, as recently as March, bragged about the fact that he is a deregulator.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: On the other hand, two years ago, I said that we’ve got a sub-prime lending crisis that has to be dealt with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I wrote to Secretary Paulson, I wrote to Federal Reserve Chairman Bernanke, and told them this is something we have to deal with, and nobody did anything about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: A year ago, I went to Wall Street and said we’ve got to reregulate, and nothing happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And Senator McCain during that period said that we should keep on deregulating because that’s how the free enterprise system works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, with respect to Fannie Mae, what Senator McCain didn’t mention is the fact that this bill that he talked about wasn’t his own bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He jumped on it a year after it had been introduced and it never got passed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I never promoted Fannie Mae.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, Senator McCain’s campaign chairman’s firm was a lobbyist on behalf of Fannie Mae, not me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So — but, look, you’re not interested in hearing politicians pointing fingers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What you’re interested in is trying to figure out, how is this going to impact you?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is not the end of the process; this is the beginning of the process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why it’s going to be so important for us to work with homeowners to make sure that they can stay in their homes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The secretary already has the power to do that in the rescue package, but it hasn’t been exercised yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the next president has to make sure that the next Treasury secretary is thinking about how to strengthen you as a home buyer, you as a homeowner, and not simply think about bailing out banks on Wall Street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, I am confident about the American economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we are going to have to have some leadership from Washington that not only sets out much better regulations for the financial system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The problem is we still have a archaic, 20th-century regulatory system for 21st-century financial markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to coordinate with other countries to make sure that whatever actions we take work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But most importantly, we’re going to have to help ordinary families be able to stay in their homes, make sure that they can pay their bills, deal with critical issues like health care and energy, and we’re going to have to change the culture in Washington so that lobbyists and special interests aren’t driving the process and your voices aren’t being drowned out.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think it depends on what we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think if we act effectively, if we stabilize the housing market — which I believe we can, if we go out and buy up these bad loans, so that people can have a new mortgage at the new value of their home — I think if we get rid of the cronyism and special interest influence in Washington so we can act more effectively.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friend, I’d like you to see the letter that a group of senators and I wrote warning exactly of this crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama’s name was not on that letter.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The point is — the point is that we can fix our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Americans’ workers are the best in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re the fundamental aspect of America’s economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re the most innovative.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re the best — they’re most — have best — we’re the best exporters.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re the best importers.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re most effective.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They are the best workers in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to give them a chance.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’ve got — we’ve got to give them a chance to do their best again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they are the innocent bystanders here in what is the biggest financial crisis and challenge of our time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, look, I understand your frustration and your cynicism, because while you’ve been carrying out your responsibilities — most of the people here, you’ve got a family budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If less money is coming in, you end up making cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Maybe you don’t go out to dinner as much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Maybe you put off buying a new car.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what happens in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you’re right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There is a lot of blame to go around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I think it’s important just to remember a little bit of history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When George Bush came into office, we had surpluses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And now we have half-a-trillion-dollar deficit annually.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When George Bush came into office, our debt — national debt was around $5 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s now over $10 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve almost doubled it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so while it’s true that nobody’s completely innocent here, we have had over the last eight years the biggest increases in deficit spending and national debt in our history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And Senator McCain voted for four out of five of those George Bush budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So here’s what I would do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to spend some money on the key issues that we’ve got to work on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, you may have seen your health care premiums go up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to reform health care to help you and your budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are going to have to deal with energy because we can’t keep on borrowing from the Chinese and sending money to Saudi Arabia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are mortgaging our children’s future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to have a different energy plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to invest in college affordability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we’re going to have to make some investments, but we’ve also got to make spending cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I’ve proposed, you’ll hear Senator McCain say, well, he’s proposing a whole bunch of new spending, but actually I’m cutting more than I’m spending so that it will be a net spending cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The key is whether or not we’ve got priorities that are working for you as opposed to those who have been dictating the policy in Washington lately, and that’s mostly lobbyists and special interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to put an end to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, Theresa , thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I can see why you feel that cynicism and mistrust, because the system in Washington is broken.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I have been a consistent reformer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have advocated and taken on the special interests, whether they be the big money people by reaching across the aisle and working with Senator Feingold on campaign finance reform, whether it being a variety of other issues, working with Senator Lieberman on trying to address climate change.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have a clear record of bipartisanship.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The situation today cries out for bipartisanship.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has never taken on his leaders of his party on a single issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we need to reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And so let’s look at our records as well as our rhetoric.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s really part of your mistrust here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And now I suggest that maybe you go to some of these organizations that are the watchdogs of what we do, like the Citizens Against Government Waste or the National Taxpayers Union or these other organizations that watch us all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t expect you to watch every vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And you know what you’ll find?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This is the most liberal big-spending record in the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought against excessive spending and outrages.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought to reduce the earmarks and eliminate them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Do you know that Senator Obama has voted for — is proposing $860 billion of new spending now?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: New spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Do you know that he voted for every increase in spending that I saw come across the floor of the United States Senate while we were working to eliminate these pork barrel earmarks?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He voted for nearly a billion dollars in pork barrel earmark projects, including, by the way, $3 million for an overhead projector at a planetarium in Chicago, Illinois.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friends, do we need to spend that kind of money?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think you have to look at my record and you have to look at his.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Then you have to look at our proposals for our economy, not $860 billion in new spending, but for the kinds of reforms that keep people in their jobs, get middle-income Americans working again, and getting our economy moving again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to be examining our proposals tonight and in the future, and energy independence is a way to do that, is one of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And drilling offshore and nuclear power are two vital elements of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve been supporting those and I know how to fix this economy, and eliminate our dependence on foreign oil, and stop sending $700 billion a year overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The three priorities were health…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think you can work on all three at once, Tom.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s very important that we reform our entitlement programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friends, we are not going to be able to provide the same benefit for present-day workers that we are going — that present-day retirees have today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to sit down across the table, Republican and Democrat, as we did in 1983 between Ronald Reagan and Tip O’Neill.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know how to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have a clear record of reaching across the aisle, whether it be Joe Lieberman or Russ Feingold or Ted Kennedy or others.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s my clear record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can work on nuclear power plants.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Build a whole bunch of them, create millions of new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to have all of the above, alternative fuels, wind, tide, solar, natural gas, clean coal technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: All of these things we can do as Americans and we can take on this mission and we can overcome it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friends, some of this $700 billion ends up in the hands of terrorist organizations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As far as health care is concerned, obviously, everyone is struggling to make sure that they can afford their premiums and that they can have affordable and available health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s the next issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we can do them all at once.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There’s no — and we have to do them all at once.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: All three you mentioned are compelling national security requirements.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to prioritize, just like a family has to prioritize.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’ve listed the things that I think have to be at the top of the list.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Energy we have to deal with today, because you’re paying $3.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: 80 here in Nashville for gasoline, and it could go up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it’s a strain on your family budget, but it’s also bad for our national security, because countries like Russia and Venezuela and, you know, in some cases, countries like Iran, are benefiting from higher oil prices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to deal with that right away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I’ve called for an investment of $15 billion a year over 10 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Our goal should be, in 10 year’s time, we are free of dependence on Middle Eastern oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we can do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, when JFK said we’re going to the Moon in 10 years, nobody was sure how to do it, but we understood that, if the American people make a decision to do something, it gets done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So that would be priority number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Health care is priority number two, because that broken health care system is bad not only for families, but it’s making our businesses less competitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, number three, we’ve got to deal with education so that our young people are competitive in a global economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But just one point I want to make, Tom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain mentioned looking at our records.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We do need to look at our records.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain likes to talk about earmarks a lot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to go line by line through every item in the federal budget and eliminate programs that don’t work and make sure that those that do work, work better and cheaper.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But understand this: We also have to look at where some of our tax revenues are going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So when Senator McCain proposes a $300 billion tax cut, a continuation not only of the Bush tax cuts, but an additional $200 billion that he’s going to give to big corporations, including big oil companies, $4 billion worth, that’s money out of the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so we’ve got to prioritize both our spending side and our tax policies to make sure that they’re working for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I’m going to do as president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, Fiora , I’m going to ask the American people to understand that there are some programs that we may have to eliminate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I first proposed a long time ago that we would have to examine every agency and every bureaucracy of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to have to eliminate those that aren’t working.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know a lot of them that aren’t working.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: One of them is in defense spending, because I’ve taken on some of the defense contractors.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I saved the taxpayers $6.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: 8 billion in a deal for an Air Force tanker that was done in a corrupt fashion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I believe that we have to eliminate the earmarks.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And sometimes those projects, not — not the overhead projector that Senator Obama asked for, but some of them that are really good projects, will have — will have to be eliminated, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they’ll have to undergo the same scrutiny that all projects should in competition with others.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So we’re going to have to tell the American people that spending is going to have to be cut in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I recommend a spending freeze that — except for defense, Veterans Affairs, and some other vital programs, we’ll just have to have across-the-board freeze.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And some of those programs may not grow as much as we would like for them to, but we can establish priorities with full transparency, with full knowledge of the American people, and full consultation, not done behind closed doors and shoving earmarks in the middle of the night into programs that we don’t even — sometimes we don’t even know about until months later.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way, I want to go back a second.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, we can attack health care and energy at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re not — we’re not — we’re not rifle shots here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We are Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can, with the participation of all Americans, work together and solve these problems together.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Frankly, I’m not going to tell that person without health insurance that, “I’m sorry, you’ll have to wait.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” I’m going to tell you Americans we’ll get to work right away and we’ll get to work together, and we can get them all done, because that’s what America has been doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, a lot of you remember the tragedy of 9/11 and where you were on that day and, you know, how all of the country was ready to come together and make enormous changes to make us not only safer, but to make us a better country and a more unified country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And President Bush did some smart things at the outset, but one of the opportunities that was missed was, when he spoke to the American people, he said, “Go out and shop.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” That wasn’t the kind of call to service that I think the American people were looking for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so it’s important to understand that the — I think the American people are hungry for the kind of leadership that is going to tackle these problems not just in government, but outside of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And let’s take the example of energy, which we already spoke about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There is going to be the need for each and every one of us to start thinking about how we use energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I believe in the need for increased oil production.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to explore new ways to get more oil, and that includes offshore drilling.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It includes telling the oil companies, that currently have 68 million acres that they’re not using, that either you use them or you lose them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to develop clean coal technology and safe ways to store nuclear energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But each and every one of us can start thinking about how can we save energy in our homes, in our buildings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things I want to do is make sure that we’re providing incentives so that you can buy a fuel efficient car that’s made right here in the United States of America, not in Japan or South Korea, making sure that you are able to weatherize your home or make your business more fuel efficient.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s going to require effort from each and every one of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the last point I just want to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think the young people of America are especially interested in how they can serve, and that’s one of the reasons why I’m interested in doubling the Peace Corps, making sure that we are creating a volunteer corps all across this country that can be involved in their community, involved in military service, so that military families and our troops are not the only ones bearing the burden of renewing America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s something that all of us have to be involved with and that requires some leadership from Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think it starts with Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to show that we’ve got good habits, because if we’re running up trillion dollar debts that we’re passing on to the next generation, then a lot of people are going to think, “Well, you know what?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s easy money out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” It means — and I have to, again, repeat this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It means looking at the spending side, but also at the revenue side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean, Senator McCain has been talking tough about earmarks, and that’s good, but earmarks account for about $18 billion of our budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, when Senator McCain is proposing tax cuts that would give the average Fortune 500 CEO an additional $700,000 in tax cuts, that’s not sharing a burden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so part of the problem, I think, for a lot of people who are listening here tonight is they don’t feel as if they are sharing the burden with other folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean, you know, it’s tough to ask a teacher who’s making $30,000 or $35,000 a year to tighten her belt when people who are making much more than her are living pretty high on the hog.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I think it’s important for the president to set a tone that says all of us are going to contribute, all of us are going to make sacrifices, and it means that, yes, we may have to cut some spending, although I disagree with Senator McCain about an across-the- board freeze.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s an example of an unfair burden sharing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s using a hatchet to cut the federal budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to use a scalpel so that people who need help are getting help and those of us, like myself and Senator McCain, who don’t need help, aren’t getting it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we make sure that everybody is willing to make a few sacrifices.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, you know, nailing down Senator Obama’s various tax proposals is like nailing Jell-O to the wall.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There has been five or six of them and if you wait long enough, there will probably be another one.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But he wants to raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friends, the last president to raise taxes during tough economic times was Herbert Hoover, and he practiced protectionism as well, which I’m sure we’ll get to at some point.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, last year up to this time, we’ve lost 700,000 jobs in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The only bright spot is that over 300,000 jobs have been created by small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama’s secret that you don’t know is that his tax increases will increase taxes on 50 percent of small business revenue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Small businesses across America will have to cut jobs and will have their taxes increase and won’t be able to hire because of Senator Obama’s tax policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, he said some time ago, he said he would forgo his tax increases if the economy was bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got some news, Senator Obama, the news is bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So let’s not raise anybody’s taxes, my friends, and make it be very clear to you I am not in favor of tax cuts for the wealthy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I am in favor of leaving the tax rates alone and reducing the tax burden on middle-income Americans by doubling your tax exemption for every child from $3,500 to $7,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: To giving every American a $5,000 refundable tax credit and go out and get the health insurance you want rather than mandates and fines for small businesses, as Senator Obama’s plan calls for.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And let’s create jobs and let’s get our economy going again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And let’s not raise anybody’s taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Tom, can I respond to this briefly?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The tax issue, because I think it’s very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Go ahead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Tom, we’re going to have to take on entitlements and I think we’ve got to do it quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have a lot of work to do, so I can’t guarantee that we’re going to do it in the next two years, but I’d like to do in the my first term as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I think it’s important to understand, we’re not going to solve Social Security and Medicare unless we understand the rest of our tax policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you know, Senator McCain, I think the “Straight Talk Express” lost a wheel on that one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So let’s be clear about my tax plan and Senator McCain’s, because we’re not going to be able to deal with entitlements unless we understand the revenues coming in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to provide a tax cut for 95 percent of Americans, 95 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you make less than a quarter of a million dollars a year, you will not see a single dime of your taxes go up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you make $200,000 a year or less, your taxes will go down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator McCain talks about small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Only a few percent of small businesses make more than $250,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So the vast majority of small businesses would get a tax cut under my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we provide a 50 percent tax credit so that they can buy health insurance for their workers, because there are an awful lot of small businesses that I meet across America that want to do right by their workers but they just can’t afford it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Some small business owners, a lot of them, can’t even afford health insurance for themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, in contrast, Senator McCain wants to give a $300 billion tax cut, $200 billion of it to the largest corporations and a hundred thousand of it — a hundred billion of it going to people like CEOs on Wall Street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He wants to give average Fortune 500 CEO an additional $700,000 in tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is not fair.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, if we get our tax policies right so that they’re good for the middle class, if we reverse the policies of the last eight years that got us into this fix in the first place and that Senator McCain supported, then we are going to be in a position to deal with Social Security and deal with Medicare, because we will have a health care plan that actually works for you, reduces spending and costs over the long term, and Social Security that is stable and solvent for all Americans and not just some.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Hey, I’ll answer the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look — look, it’s not that hard to fix Social Security, Tom.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s just…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: … tough decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to get to Medicare in a second.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Social Security is not that tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We know what the problems are, my friends, and we know what the fixes are.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to sit down together across the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s been done before.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I saw it done with our — our wonderful Ronald Reagan, a conservative from California, and the liberal Democrat Tip O’Neill from Massachusetts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we need more of, and that’s what I’ve done in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has never taken on his party leaders on a single major issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve taken them on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m not too popular sometimes with my own party, much less his.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So Medicare, it’s going to be a little tougher.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to be a little tougher because we’re talking about very complex and difficult issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friends, what we have to do with Medicare is have a commission, have the smartest people in America come together, come up with recommendations, and then, like the base-closing commission idea we had, then we should have Congress vote up or down.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s not let them fool with it anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There’s too much special interests and too many lobbyists working there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So let’s have — and let’s have the American people say, “Fix it for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” Now, just back on this — on this tax, you know, again, it’s back to our first question here about rhetoric and record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has voted 94 times to either increase your taxes or against tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s his record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: When he ran for the United States Senate from Illinois, he said he would have a middle-income tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know he came to the Senate and never once proposed legislation to do that?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So let’s look at our record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve fought higher taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought excess spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought to reform government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s look at our records, my friends, and then listen to my vision for the future of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll get our economy going again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And our best days are ahead of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, we are in tough economic times; we all know that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And let’s keep — never forget the struggle that Americans are in today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But when we can — when we have an issue that we may hand our children and our grandchildren a damaged planet, I have disagreed strongly with the Bush administration on this issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I traveled all over the world looking at the effects of greenhouse gas emissions, Joe Lieberman and I.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I introduced the first legislation, and we forced votes on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s the good news, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The bad news is we lost.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we kept the debate going, and we kept this issue to — to posing to Americans the danger that climate change opposes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, how — what’s — what’s the best way of fixing it?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Nuclear power.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama says that it has to be safe or disposable or something like that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, I — I was on Navy ships that had nuclear power plants.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Nuclear power is safe, and it’s clean, and it creates hundreds of thousands of jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And — and I know that we can reprocess the spent nuclear fuel.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The Japanese, the British, the French do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we can do it, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has opposed that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can move forward, and clean up our climate, and develop green technologies, and alternate — alternative energies for — for hybrid, for hydrogen, for battery-powered cars, so that we can clean up our environment and at the same time get our economy going by creating millions of jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can do that, we as Americans, because we’re the best innovators, we’re the best producers, and 95 percent of the people who are our market live outside of the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is one of the biggest challenges of our times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it is absolutely critical that we understand this is not just a challenge, it’s an opportunity, because if we create a new energy economy, we can create five million new jobs, easily, here in the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It can be an engine that drives us into the future the same way the computer was the engine for economic growth over the last couple of decades.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we can do it, but we’re going to have to make an investment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The same way the computer was originally invented by a bunch of government scientists who were trying to figure out, for defense purposes, how to communicate, we’ve got to understand that this is a national security issue, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why we’ve got to make some investments and I’ve called for investments in solar, wind, geothermal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Contrary to what Senator McCain keeps on saying, I favor nuclear power as one component of our overall energy mix.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But this is another example where I think it is important to look at the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain and I actually agree on something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He said a while back that the big problem with energy is that for 30 years, politicians in Washington haven’t done anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What Senator McCain doesn’t mention is he’s been there 26 of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And during that time, he voted 23 times against alternative fuels, 23 times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So it’s easy to talk about this stuff during a campaign, but it’s important for us to understand that it requires a sustained effort from the next president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: One last point I want to make on energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain talks a lot about drilling, and that’s important, but we have three percent of the world’s oil reserves and we use 25 percent of the world’s oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what that means is that we can’t simply drill our way out of the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’re not going to be able to deal with the climate crisis if our only solution is to use more fossil fuels that create global warming.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to come up with alternatives, and that means that the United States government is working with the private sector to fund the kind of innovation that we can then export to countries like China that also need energy and are setting up one coal power plant a week.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to make sure that we’re giving them the energy that they need or helping them to create the energy that they need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m just trying to keep up with John.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Tom, wave like that and I’ll look at you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think pure research and development investment on the part of the United States government is certainly appropriate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think once it gets into productive stages, that we ought to, obviously, turn it over to the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: By the way, my friends, I know you grow a little weary with this back-and-forth.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It was an energy bill on the floor of the Senate loaded down with goodies, billions for the oil companies, and it was sponsored by Bush and Cheney.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know who voted for it?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You might never know.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That one.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know who voted against it?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Me.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought time after time against these pork barrel — these bills that come to the floor and they have all kinds of goodies and all kinds of things in them for everybody and they buy off the votes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I vote against them, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I vote against them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the point is, also, on oil drilling, oil drilling offshore now is vital so that we can bridge the gap.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can bridge the gap between imported oil, which is a national security issue, as well as any other, and it will reduce the price of a barrel of oil, because when people know there’s a greater supply, then the cost of that will go down.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s fundamental economics.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to drill offshore, my friends, and we’ve got to do it now, and we can do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And as far as nuclear power is concerned, again, look at the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has approved storage and reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll stop, Tom, and you didn’t even wave.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thanks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, you know, as I travel around the country, this is one of the single most frequently asked issues that I get, is the issue of health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is breaking family budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I can’t tell you how many people I meet who don’t have health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you’ve got health insurance, most of you have seen your premiums double over the last eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And your co-payments and deductibles have gone up 30 percent just in the last year alone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you’re a small business, it’s a crushing burden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So one of the things that I have said from the start of this campaign is that we have a moral commitment as well as an economic imperative to do something about the health care crisis that so many families are facing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So here’s what I would do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you’ve got health care already, and probably the majority of you do, then you can keep your plan if you are satisfied with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You can keep your choice of doctor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to work with your employer to lower the cost of your premiums by up to $2,500 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to do it by investing in prevention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to do it by making sure that we use information technology so that medical records are actually on computers instead of you filling forms out in triplicate when you go to the hospital.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That will reduce medical errors and reduce costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t have health insurance, you’re going to be able to buy the same kind of insurance that Senator McCain and I enjoy as federal employees.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because there’s a huge pool, we can drop the costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And nobody will be excluded for pre-existing conditions, which is a huge problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator McCain has a different kind of approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He says that he’s going to give you a $5,000 tax credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What he doesn’t tell you is that he is going to tax your employer-based health care benefits for the first time ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what one hand giveth, the other hand taketh away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He would also strip away the ability of states to provide some of the regulations on insurance companies to make sure you’re not excluded for pre-existing conditions or your mammograms are covered or your maternity is covered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that is fundamentally the wrong way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, just today business organizations like the United States Chamber of Commerce, which generally are pretty supportive of Republicans, said that this would lead to the unraveling of the employer-based health care system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That, I don’t think, is the kind of change that we need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to have somebody who is fighting for patients and making sure that you get decent, affordable health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s something that I’m committed to doing as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you for the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You really identified one of the really major challenges that America faces.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Co-payments go up, costs go up, skyrocketing costs, which make people less and less able to afford health insurance in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we need to do all of the things that are necessary to make it more efficient.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s put health records online, that will reduce medical errors, as they call them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s have community health centers.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s have walk-in clinics.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s do a lot of things to impose efficiencies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But what is at stake here in this health care issue is the fundamental difference between myself and Senator Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As you notice, he starts talking about government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He starts saying, government will do this and government will do that, and then government will, and he’ll impose mandates.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If you’re a small business person and you don’t insure your employees, Senator Obama will fine you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Will fine you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s remarkable.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If you’re a parent and you’re struggling to get health insurance for your children, Senator Obama will fine you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to give every American a $5,000 refundable tax credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They can take it anywhere, across state lines.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Why not?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Don’t we go across state lines when we purchase other things in America?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course it’s OK to go across state lines because in Arizona they may offer a better plan that suits you best than it does here in Tennessee.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And if you do the math, those people who have employer-based health benefits, if you put the tax on it and you have what’s left over and you add $5,000 that you’re going to get as a refundable tax credit, do the math, 95 percent of the American people will have increased funds to go out and buy the insurance of their choice and to shop around and to get — all of those people will be covered except for those who have these gold-plated Cadillac kinds of policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, like hair transplants, I might need one of those myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the point is that we have got to give people choice in America and not mandate things on them and give them the ability.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Every parent I know would acquire health insurance for their children if they could.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Obviously small business people want to give their employees health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course they all want to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to give them the wherewithal to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can do it by giving them, as a start, a $5,000 refundable tax credit to go around and get the health insurance policy of their choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s a responsibility, in this respect, in that we should have available and affordable health care to every American citizen, to every family member.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And with the plan that — that I have, that will do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But government mandates I — I’m always a little nervous about.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But it is certainly my responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It is certainly small-business people and others, and they understand that responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: American citizens understand that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Employers understand that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But they certainly are a little nervous when Senator Obama says, if you don’t get the health care policy that I think you should have, then you’re going to get fined.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way, Senator Obama has never mentioned how much that fine might be.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Perhaps we might find that out tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, why don’t — why don’t — let’s talk about this, Tom, because there was just a lot of stuff out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think it should be a right for every American.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In a country as wealthy as ours, for us to have people who are going bankrupt because they can’t pay their medical bills — for my mother to die of cancer at the age of 53 and have to spend the last months of her life in the hospital room arguing with insurance companies because they’re saying that this may be a pre-existing condition and they don’t have to pay her treatment, there’s something fundamentally wrong about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So let me — let me just talk about this fundamental difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, Tom, I know that we’re under time constraints, but Senator McCain through a lot of stuff out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one, let me just repeat, if you’ve got a health care plan that you like, you can keep it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: All I’m going to do is help you to lower the premiums on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’ll still have choice of doctor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s no mandate involved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Small businesses are not going to have a mandate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we’re going to give you is a 50 percent tax credit to help provide health care for those that you need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, it’s true that I say that you are going to have to make sure that your child has health care, because children are relatively cheap to insure and we don’t want them going to the emergency room for treatable illnesses like asthma.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when Senator McCain says that he wants to provide children health care, what he doesn’t mention is he voted against the expansion of the Children’s Health Insurance Program that is responsible for making sure that so many children who didn’t have previously health insurance have it now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, the final point I’ll make on this whole issue of government intrusion and mandates — it is absolutely true that I think it is important for government to crack down on insurance companies that are cheating their customers, that don’t give you the fine print, so you end up thinking that you’re paying for something and, when you finally get sick and you need it, you’re not getting it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason that it’s a problem to go shopping state by state, you know what insurance companies will do?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They will find a state — maybe Arizona, maybe another state — where there are no requirements for you to get cancer screenings, where there are no requirements for you to have to get pre-existing conditions, and they will all set up shop there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how in banking it works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Everybody goes to Delaware, because they’ve got very — pretty loose laws when it comes to things like credit cards.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And in that situation, what happens is, is that the protections you have, the consumer protections that you need, you’re not going to have available to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is a fundamental difference that I have with Senator McCain.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He believes in deregulation in every circumstance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we’ve been going through for the last eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It hasn’t worked, and we need fundamental change.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe that — did we hear the size of the fine?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, I thank you for that question, because there’s no doubt that history shows us that nations that are strong militarily over time have to have a strong economy, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that is one of the challenges that America faces.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But having said that, America — and we’ll hear a lot of criticism.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve heard a lot of criticism about America, and our national security policy, and all that, and much of that criticism is justified.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the fact is, America is the greatest force for good in the history of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friends, we have gone to all four corners of the Earth and shed American blood in defense, usually, of somebody else’s freedom and our own.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So we are peacemakers and we’re peacekeepers.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the challenge is to know when the United States of American can beneficially effect the outcome of a crisis, when to go in and when not, when American military power is worth the expenditure of our most precious treasure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that question can only be answered by someone with the knowledge and experience and the judgment, the judgment to know when our national security is not only at risk, but where the United States of America can make a difference in preventing genocide, in preventing the spread of terrorism, in doing the things that the United States has done, not always well, but we’ve done because we’re a nation of good.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
