transcript_turns.text: And I am convinced that my record, going back to my opposition from sending the Marines to Lebanon, to supporting our efforts in Kosovo and Bosnia and the first Gulf War, and my judgment, I think, is something that I’m — a record that I’m willing to stand on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama was wrong about Iraq and the surge.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He was wrong about Russia when they committed aggression against Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And in his short career, he does not understand our national security challenges.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have time for on-the-job training, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, you know, Senator McCain, in the last debate and today, again, suggested that I don’t understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There are some things I don’t understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I don’t understand how we ended up invading a country that had nothing to do with 9/11, while Osama Bin Laden and Al Qaeda are setting up base camps and safe havens to train terrorists to attack us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That was Senator McCain’s judgment and it was the wrong judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When Senator McCain was cheerleading the president to go into Iraq, he suggested it was going to be quick and easy, we’d be greeted as liberators.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That was the wrong judgment, and it’s been costly to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So one of the difficulties with Iraq is that it has put an enormous strain, first of all, on our troops, obviously, and they have performed heroically and honorably and we owe them an extraordinary debt of gratitude.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it’s also put an enormous strain on our budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve spent, so far, close to $700 billion and if we continue on the path that we’re on, as Senator McCain is suggesting, it’s going to go well over $1 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re spending $10 billion a month in Iraq at a time when the Iraqis have a $79 billion surplus, $79 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we need that $10 billion a month here in the United States to put people back to work, to do all these wonderful things that Senator McCain suggested we should be doing, but has not yet explained how he would pay for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator McCain and I do agree, this is the greatest nation on earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are a force of good in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there has never been a nation in the history of the world that saw its economy decline and maintained its military superiority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the strains that have been placed on our alliances around the world and the respect that’s been diminished over the last eight years has constrained us being able to act on something like the genocide in Darfur, because we don’t have the resources or the allies to do everything that we should be doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to change when I’m president, but we can’t change it unless we fundamentally change Senator McCain’s and George Bush’s foreign policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It has not worked for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, we may not always have national security issues at stake, but we have moral issues at stake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we could have intervened effectively in the Holocaust, who among us would say that we had a moral obligation not to go in?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we could’ve stopped Rwanda, surely, if we had the ability, that would be something that we would have to strongly consider and act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So when genocide is happening, when ethnic cleansing is happening somewhere around the world and we stand idly by, that diminishes us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so I do believe that we have to consider it as part of our interests, our national interests, in intervening where possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But understand that there’s a lot of cruelty around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to be able to be everywhere all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why it’s so important for us to be able to work in concert with our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s take the example of Darfur just for a moment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Right now there’s a peacekeeping force that has been set up and we have African Union troops in Darfur to stop a genocide that has killed hundreds of thousands of people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We could be providing logistical support, setting up a no-fly zone at relatively little cost to us, but we can only do it if we can help mobilize the international community and lead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what I intend to do when I’m president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just follow up, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If we had done what Senator Obama wanted done in Iraq, and that was set a date for withdrawal, which General Petraeus, our chief — chairman of our Joint Chiefs of Staff said would be a very dangerous course to take for America, then we would have had a wider war, we would have been back, Iranian influence would have increased, al Qaeda would have re- established a base.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There was a lot at stake there, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I can tell you right now that Senator Obama would have brought our troops home in defeat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ll bring them home with victory and with honor and that is a fundamental difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The United States of America, Tom, is the greatest force for good, as I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we must do whatever we can to prevent genocide, whatever we can to prevent these terrible calamities that we have said never again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But it also has to be tempered with our ability to beneficially affect the situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That requires a cool hand at the tiller.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This requires a person who understands what our — the limits of our capability are.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We went in to Somalia as a peacemaking organization, we ended up trying to be — excuse me, as a peacekeeping organization, we ended up trying to be peacemakers and we ended up having to withdraw in humiliation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: In Lebanon, I stood up to President Reagan, my hero, and said, if we send Marines in there, how can we possibly beneficially affect this situation?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And said we shouldn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, almost 300 brave young Marines were killed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So you have to temper your decisions with the ability to beneficially affect the situation and realize you’re sending America’s most precious asset, American blood, into harm’s way.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, again, I know those situations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been in them all my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I can tell you right now the security of your young men and women who are serving in the military are my first priority right after our nation’s security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I may have to make those tough decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I won’t take them lightly.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I understand that we have to say never again to a Holocaust and never again to Rwanda.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we had also better be darn sure we don’t leave and make the situation worse, thereby exacerbating our reputation and our ability to address crises in other parts of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Katie, it’s a terrific question and we have a difficult situation in Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I believe that part of the reason we have a difficult situation is because we made a bad judgment going into Iraq in the first place when we hadn’t finished the job of hunting down bin Laden and crushing al Qaeda.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what happened was we got distracted, we diverted resources, and ultimately bin Laden escaped, set up base camps in the mountains of Pakistan in the northwest provinces there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are now raiding our troops in Afghanistan, destabilizing the situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’re stronger now than at any time since 2001.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I think it’s so important for us to reverse course, because that’s the central front on terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are plotting to kill Americans right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: As Secretary Gates, the defense secretary, said, the war against terrorism began in that region and that’s where it will end.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So part of the reason I think it’s so important for us to end the war in Iraq is to be able to get more troops into Afghanistan, put more pressure on the Afghan government to do what it needs to do, eliminate some of the drug trafficking that’s funding terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I do believe that we have to change our policies with Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can’t coddle, as we did, a dictator, give him billions of dollars and then he’s making peace treaties with the Taliban and militants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I’ve said is we’re going to encourage democracy in Pakistan, expand our nonmilitary aid to Pakistan so that they have more of a stake in working with us, but insisting that they go after these militants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we have Osama bin Laden in our sights and the Pakistani government is unable or unwilling to take them out, then I think that we have to act and we will take them out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We will kill bin Laden; we will crush Al Qaida.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That has to be our biggest national security priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, Katie , thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, my hero is a guy named Teddy Roosevelt.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Teddy Roosevelt used to say walk softly — talk softly, but carry a big stick.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama likes to talk loudly.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: In fact, he said he wants to announce that he’s going to attack Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Remarkable.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, if you are a country and you’re trying to gain the support of another country, then you want to do everything you can that they would act in a cooperative fashion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: When you announce that you’re going to launch an attack into another country, it’s pretty obvious that you have the effect that it had in Pakistan: It turns public opinion against us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, let me just go back with you very briefly.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We drove the Russians out with — the Afghan freedom fighters drove the Russians out of Afghanistan, and then we made a most serious mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We washed our hands of Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The Taliban came back in, Al Qaida, we then had the situation that required us to conduct the Afghan war.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, our relations with Pakistan are critical, because the border areas are being used as safe havens by the Taliban and Al Qaida and other extremist organizations, and we have to get their support.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, General Petraeus had a strategy, the same strategy — very, very different, because of the conditions and the situation — but the same fundamental strategy that succeeded in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that is to get the support of the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to help the Pakistani government go into Waziristan, where I visited, a very rough country, and — and get the support of the people, and get them to work with us and turn against the cruel Taliban and others.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And by working and coordinating our efforts together, not threatening to attack them, but working with them, and where necessary use force, but talk softly, but carry a big stick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Tom, just a…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … just a quick follow-up on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If we’re going to have follow-ups, then I will want follow-ups, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’d be fine with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’d be fine with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Then let’s have one.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’d be fine with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Just — just — just a quick follow-up, because I think — I think this is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’re doing a great job, Tom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, I — I want to be very clear about what I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nobody called for the invasion of Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain continues to repeat this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I said was the same thing that the audience here today heard me say, which is, if Pakistan is unable or unwilling to hunt down bin Laden and take him out, then we should.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, that I think has to be our policy, because they are threatening to kill more Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator McCain suggests that somehow, you know, I’m green behind the ears and, you know, I’m just spouting off, and he’s somber and responsible.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain, this is the guy who sang, “Bomb, bomb, bomb Iran,” who called for the annihilation of North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That I don’t think is an example of “speaking softly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” This is the person who, after we had — we hadn’t even finished Afghanistan, where he said, “Next up, Baghdad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” So I agree that we have to speak responsibly and we have to act responsibly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason Pakistan — the popular opinion of America had diminished in Pakistan was because we were supporting a dictator, Musharraf, had given him $10 billion over seven years, and he had suspended civil liberties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We were not promoting democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is the kind of policies that ultimately end up undermining our ability to fight the war on terrorism, and it will change when I’m president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, Tom, if — if we’re going to go back and forth, I then — I’d like to have equal time to go — to respond to…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: … to — to — to…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have, obviously, supported those efforts that the United States had to go in militarily and I have opposed that I didn’t think so.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I understand what it’s like to send young American’s in harm’s way.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I say — I was joking with a veteran — I hate to even go into this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I was joking with an old veteran friend, who joked with me, about Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the point is that I know how to handle these crises.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Senator Obama, by saying that he would attack Pakistan, look at the context of his words.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get Osama bin Laden, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get him.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know how to get him.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get him no matter what and I know how to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I’m not going to telegraph my punches, which is what Senator Obama did.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’m going to act responsibly, as I have acted responsibly throughout my military career and throughout my career in the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we have fundamental disagreements about the use of military power and how you do it, and you just saw it in response to previous questions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ll be very brief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are going to have to make the Iraqi government start taking more responsibility, withdraw our troops in a responsible way over time, because we’re going to have to put some additional troops in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: General McKiernan, the commander in Afghanistan right now, is desperate for more help, because our bases and outposts are now targets for more aggressive Afghan — Taliban offenses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re also going to have to work with the Karzai government, and when I met with President Karzai, I was very clear that, “You are going to have to do better by your people in order for us to gain the popular support that’s necessary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” I don’t think he has to be a dictator.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we want a democracy in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we have to have a government that is responsive to the Afghan people, and, frankly, it’s just not responsive right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: General Petraeus has just taken over a position of responsibility, where he has the command and will really set the tone for the strategy and tactics that are used.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve had conversations with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It is the same overall strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course, we have to do some things tactically, some of which Senator Obama is correct on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to double the size of the Afghan army.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to have a streamlined NATO command structure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to do a lot of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to work much more closely with the Pakistanis.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But most importantly, we have to have the same strategy, which Senator Obama said wouldn’t work, couldn’t work, still fails to admit that he was wrong about Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He still will not admit that he was wrong about the strategy of the surge in Iraq, and that’s the same kind of strategy of go out and secure and hold and allow people to live normal lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And once they feel secure, then they lead normal, social, economic, political lives, the same thing that’s happening in Iraq today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I have confidence that General Petraeus, working with the Pakistanis, working with the Afghans, doing the same job that he did in Iraq, will again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We will succeed and we will bring our troops home with honor and victory and not in defeat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: First of all, as I say, I don’t think that — we’re not going to have another Cold War with Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But have no doubt that Russia’s behavior is certainly outside the norms of behavior that we would expect for nations which are very wealthy, as Russia has become, because of their petro dollars.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, long ago, I warned about Vladimir Putin.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I said I looked into his eyes and saw three letters, a K, a G and a B.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He has surrounded himself with former KGB apparatchiks.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He has gradually repressed most of the liberties that we would expect for nations to observe, and he has exhibited most aggressive behavior, obviously, in Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I said before, watch Ukraine.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Ukraine, right now, is in the sights of Vladimir Putin, those that want to reassemble the old Soviet Union.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to show moral support for Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to show moral support for Ukraine.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to advocate for their membership in NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to make the Russians understand that there are penalties for these this kind of behavior, this kind of naked aggression into Georgia, a tiny country and a tiny democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And so, of course we want to bring international pressures to bear on Russia in hopes that that will modify and eventually change their behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, the G-8 is one of those, but there are many others.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the Russians must understand that these kinds of actions and activities are not acceptable and hopefully we will use the leverage, economic, diplomatic and others united with our allies, with our allies and friends in Europe who are equally disturbed as we are about their recent behaviors.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It will not be a re-ignition of the Cold War, but Russia is a challenge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, the resurgence of Russia is one of the central issues that we’re going to have to deal with in the next presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And for the most part I agree with Senator McCain on many of the steps that have to be taken.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we can’t just provide moral support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to provide moral support to the Poles and Estonia and Latvia and all of the nations that were former Soviet satellites.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve also got to provide them with financial and concrete assistance to help rebuild their economies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Georgia in particular is now on the brink of enormous economic challenges.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And some say that that’s what Putin intended in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The other thing we have to do, though, is we’ve got to see around the corners.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to anticipate some of these problems ahead of time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, back in April, I put out a statement saying that the situation in Georgia was unsustainable because you had Russian peacekeepers in these territories that were under dispute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you knew that if the Russians themselves were trying to obtain some of these territories or push back against Georgia, that that was not a stable situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So part of the job of the next commander-in-chief, in keeping all of you safe, is making sure that we can see some of the 21st Century challenges and anticipate them before they happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t been doing enough of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We tend to be reactive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we’ve been doing over the last eight years and that has actually made us more safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s part of what happened in Afghanistan, where we rushed into Iraq and Senator McCain and President Bush suggested that it wasn’t that important to catch bin Laden right now and that we could muddle through, and that has cost us dearly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to be much more strategic if we’re going to be able to deal with all of the challenges that we face out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one last point I want to make about Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Energy is going to be key in dealing with Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we can reduce our energy consumption, that reduces the amount of petro dollars that they have to make mischief around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That will strengthen us and weaken them when it comes to issues like Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think they’ve engaged in an evil behavior and I think that it is important that we understand they’re not the old Soviet Union but they still have nationalist impulses that I think are very dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Maybe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Depends on how we respond to Russia and it depends on a lot of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If I say yes, then that means that we’re reigniting the old Cold War.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If I say no, it ignores their behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Obviously energy is going to be a big, big factor.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Georgia and Ukraine are both major gateways of energy into Europe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that’s one of the reasons why it’s in our interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the Russians, I think we can deal with them but they’ve got to understand that they’re facing a very firm and determined United States of America that will defend our interests and that of other countries in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Terry .

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And thank you for your service to the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to say, everything I ever learned about leadership I learned from a chief petty officer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I thank you, and I thank you, my friend.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thanks for serving.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let — let — let me say that we obviously would not wait for the United Nations Security Council.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think the realities are that both Russia and China would probably pose significant obstacles.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And our challenge right now is the Iranians continue on the path to acquiring nuclear weapons, and it’s a great threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s not just a threat — threat to the state of Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s a threat to the stability of the entire Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If Iran acquires nuclear weapons, all the other countries will acquire them, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The tensions will be ratcheted up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: What would you do if you were the Israelis and the president of a country says that they are — they are determined to wipe you off the map, calls your country a stinking corpse?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator Obama without precondition wants to sit down and negotiate with them, without preconditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what he stated, again, a matter of record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure that the Iranians are put enough — that we put enough pressure on the Iranians by joining with our allies, imposing significant, tough sanctions to modify their behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I think we can do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think, joining with our allies and friends in a league of democracies, that we can effectively abridge their behavior, and hopefully they would abandon this quest that they are on for nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But, at the end of the day, my friend, I have to tell you again, and you know what it’s like to serve, and you know what it’s like to sacrifice, but we can never allow a second Holocaust to take place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Terry, first of all, we honor your service, and we’re grateful for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We cannot allow Iran to get a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It would be a game-changer in the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not only would it threaten Israel, our strongest ally in the region and one of our strongest allies in the world, but it would also create a possibility of nuclear weapons falling into the hands of terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so it’s unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I will do everything that’s required to prevent it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we will never take military options off the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it is important that we don’t provide veto power to the United Nations or anyone else in acting in our interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is important, though, for us to use all the tools at our disposal to prevent the scenario where we’ve got to make those kinds of choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I have consistently said that, if we can work more effectively with other countries diplomatically to tighten sanctions on Iran, if we can reduce our energy consumption through alternative energy, so that Iran has less money, if we can impose the kinds of sanctions that, say, for example, Iran right now imports gasoline, even though it’s an oil-producer, because its oil infrastructure has broken down, if we can prevent them from importing the gasoline that they need and the refined petroleum products, that starts changing their cost-benefit analysis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That starts putting the squeeze on them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, it is true, though, that I believe that we should have direct talks — not just with our friends, but also with our enemies — to deliver a tough, direct message to Iran that, if you don’t change your behavior, then there will be dire consequences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you do change your behavior, then it is possible for you to re-join the community of nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, it may not work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But one of the things we’ve learned is, is that when we take that approach, whether it’s in North Korea or in Iran, then we have a better chance at better outcomes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When President Bush decided we’re not going to talk to Iran, we’re not going to talk to North Korea, you know what happened?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Iran went from zero centrifuges to develop nuclear weapons to 4,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: North Korea quadrupled its nuclear capability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to try to have talks, understanding that we’re not taking military options off the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My wife, Michelle, is there and she could give you a much longer list than I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And most of the time, I learn it by asking her.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, look, the nature of the challenges that we’re going to face are immense and one of the things that we know about the presidency is that it’s never the challenges that you expect.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s the challenges that you don’t that end up consuming most of your time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But here’s what I do know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I know that I wouldn’t be standing here if it weren’t for the fact that this country gave me opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I came from very modest means.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I had a single mom and my grandparents raised me and it was because of the help of scholarships and my grandmother scrimping on things that she might have wanted to purchase and my mom, at one point, getting food stamps in order for us to put food on the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Despite all that, I was able to go to the best schools on earth and I was able to succeed in a way that I could not have succeeded anywhere else in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The same is true for Michelle and I’m sure the same is true for a lot of you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the question in this election is: are we going to pass on that same American dream to the next generation?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Over the last eight years, we’ve seen that dream diminish.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Wages and incomes have gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: People have lost their health care or are going bankrupt because they get sick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got young people who have got the grades and the will and the drive to go to college, but they just don’t have the money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we can’t expect that if we do the same things that we’ve been doing over the last eight years, that somehow we are going to have a different outcome.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need fundamental change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what’s at stake in this election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the reason I decided to run for president, and I’m hopeful that all of you are prepared to continue this extraordinary journey that we call America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’re going to have to have the courage and the sacrifice, the nerve to move in a new direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: BROKAW: Senator McCain, you get the last word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama had the opening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’re last up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Tom.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I think what I don’t know is what all of us don’t know, and that’s what’s going to happen both here at home and abroad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The challenges that we face are unprecedented.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Americans are hurting tonight in a way they have not in our generation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There are challenges around the world that are new and different and there will be different — we will be talking about countries sometime in the future that we hardly know where they are on the map, some Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So what I don’t know is what the unexpected will be.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I have spent my whole life serving this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I grew up in a family where my father was gone most of the time because he was at sea and doing our country’s business.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My mother basically raised our family.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know what it’s like in dark times.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know what it’s like to have to fight to keep one’s hope going through difficult times.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know what it’s like to rely on others for support and courage and love in tough times.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know what it’s like to have your comrades reach out to you and your neighbors and your fellow citizens and pick you up and put you back in the fight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what America’s all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I believe in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I believe in its future.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I believe in its greatness.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s been my great honor to serve it for many, many years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’m asking the American people to give me another opportunity and I’ll rest on my record, but I’ll also tell you, when times are tough, we need a steady hand at the tiller and the great honor of my life was to always put my country first.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Tom.
